source_text: Καὶ πολὺς μὲν ἔῤῥεεν ὁ πειράζων, καὶ χαλεπὸς ἦν ὁ μαχόμενος· ἀνδρειότερος δὲ ἐφαίνετο ὁ πειραζόμενος, νικῶν τὰς ἐπιχειρήσεις καὶ προσβολὰς τοῦ πονηροῦ τῷ μεγέθει τῆς διανοίας. Γνώρισμα τῆς ἀνδρείας ἐστὶν ἡ ὑπομονή. Ταύτῃ γὰρ ἕκαστος τῶν ἁγίων φέρων τὰ συμβάντα ἐν τῷ βίῳ ἐπίπονα καὶ λυπηρὰ, ἴσχυε κατὰ τοῦ διαβόλου· ἅπερ τὸ Πνεῦμα θέλον ἡμᾶς ἀμφότερα κτᾶσθαι, προστάττει λέγον ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ· Ἀνδρίζου, καὶ κραταιούσθω ἡ καρδία σου, καὶ ὑπόμεινον τὸν Κύριον. Ὁ γὰρ ὑπομένων ἀνδρεῖός ἐστι, καὶ ὁ ἀνδρεῖος ὑπομονητικὸς ἂν εἴη. Διὸ καὶ ὁ μακάριος Ἰὼβ διὰ τὸ ὑπομένειν ἐκραταιοῦτο, καὶ διὰ τὸ ἀνδρείως φέρειν τοὺς πόνους ὑπέμεινε, καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα διωθεῖτο, ἐξαπατηθεῖσαν ὑπὸ τοῦ ὄφεως, καὶ φθαρεῖσαν τὰ νοήματα. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ὅλως ἐστὶ μισητὴς ὁ τῆς κακίας εὑρετὴς, καὶ μό νον φαινόμενος ζητῶν τίνα ἁρπάσει καὶ καταπιεῖ· διὰ τοῦτο ὃ μὲν ἔστιν αὐτὸς ὑποκρύπτει καὶ σκέπει· ὑποκρινόμενος δὲ τῇ φαντασίᾳ τὴν πᾶσι ποθουμένην ἀλήθειαν, τὸν ἴδιον ἰὸν ἐπιβάλλει τοῖς ἀκολουθήσασιν αὐτῷ. Οὕτω καὶ τὴν Εὔαν ἠπάτησεν, οὐ τὰ ἴδια λαλῶν, ἀλλ' ὑποκρινόμενος τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ῥήματα, καὶ τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν παραποιῶν. Οὕτω καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ Ἰὼβ ὑπέβαλε, πείσας αὐτῇ ὑποκρίνεσθαι φιλανδρίαν, διδάξας δὲ βλασφημεῖν εἰς τὸν Θεόν. Οὕτω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὁ δόλιος παίζει ταῖς φαντασίαις ὑποκλέπτων καὶ σύρων ἕκαστον εἰς τὸν ἴδιον τῆς κακίας βόθρον. Εἰ κατὰ παίδων αὐτοῦ οὐ πιστεύει, κατὰ δὲ ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ σκολιόν τι ἐπενόησεν. Ἀθανασίου. Ἡ δὲ τῶν γεννητῶν καὶ κτιστῶν φύσις τρεπτή ἐστι, ἅτε δὴ ἔξωθεν οὖσα τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ σίας, καὶ ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ὑποστᾶσα Διὸ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης· καὶ, πάντες ἥμαρτον, καὶ ὑστεροῦνται τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ὁ δὲ διάβολος, ἐν μέσῳ τῶν χερουβὶμ ὢν, καὶ ἀποσφράγισμα ὁμοιώσεως γενόμενος, ἐξέπεσεν ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὡς ἀστραπή. Καὶ ἀγγέλους κρινοῦμεν, τοὺς μὴ τηρήσαντας δηλαδὴ τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχήν. Καὶ ἐνταῦθα, εἰ κατὰ παιδίων αὐτοῦ οὐ πιστεύει, καὶ ἁπλῶς τὰ κτίσματα τοιαύτην ἔχει τὴν φύσιν, καὶ τρέπεται. Μόνη δὲ ἡ θεία φύσις ἀναλλοίωτος. Παρὰ πάπυρον, καὶ κάλαμον, καὶ βούτομον. Τάχα δὲ διὰ τοῦ καλάμου καὶ τοῦ παπύρου τὴν εὐτέλειαν καὶ τὴν πενίαν τοῦ διαβόλου αἰνίττεται ἡ Γραφή. Τὰ ἔγκατα αὐτοῦ ἀσπίδες χάλκεαι. Ἀθανάσιος. Πάλαι μὲν οὖν πολὺς ἦν ὁ ἐχθρὸς πανουργευόμενος κατὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ φαντασίαις αὐτοῦ πολλοὺς ἠπάτα, καὶ δυσχερὴς ἦν ἡ τῆς ἀπάτης αὐτοῦ κατάληψις· ὥστε καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα λέγειν περὶ αὐτοῦ· Τίς ἀποκαλύψει πρόσωπον ἐνδύματος αὐτοῦ; καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Οὐ γὰρ ὅπερ ἦν, τοῦτο καὶ ἐφαίνετο, ἀλλὰ πρὸς ὃ ἐπανουργεύετο, πρὸς τοῦτο καὶ ἐφαντασίου ἑαυτόν. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ πολλοὶ ἠπατῶντο ὑπ' αὐτοῦ· ὅτε δὲ ἐπεδήμησεν ὁ Σωτὴρ, τότε ἡ πᾶσα φαντασία αὐτοῦ ἐδειγματίσθη· ἃ γὰρ ἠγνοεῖτο πάλαι ποιῶν, ταῦτα τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Χριστοῦ γινώσκεται, καὶ ἐν οἷς ἠπάτα πάλαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐν τούτοις ὑπ' αὐτῶν καταπατεῖται. Πάσης γὰρ διαβολικῆς ἐπιθέσεως καὶ μανίας δαιμόνων ἰσχυροτέρα ἡ πίστις.
thought_title: Endurance as courage, the devil's illusions, and the changeable nature of created things
orientation: Athanasius continues his commentary on Job, explaining that Job's endurance was the mark of his courage, then describes how the devil deceives through illusions, and finally contrasts the changeable nature of created things with the unchangeable divine nature.
pass_a_gloss: And the tempter was pouring forth abundantly, and the one fighting was harsh; but the one being tempted appeared more courageous, conquering the attempts and assaults of the evil one by the greatness of his mind. The mark of courage is endurance. For by this each of the saints, bearing the painful and grievous things that happen in life, was strong against the devil; which things the Spirit, wishing us to acquire both, commands, saying in the psalm: Be strong, and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord. For the one who endures is courageous, and the courageous one would be enduring. Therefore also the blessed Job, because of enduring, was strengthened, and because of bearing the pains courageously, he endured, and he was pushing away his wife, who had been deceived by the serpent and corrupted in her thoughts. For since the inventor of evil is altogether a hater, and only appearing, seeking whom he may seize and swallow; for this reason what he himself is he hides and covers; but pretending by illusion the truth desired by all, he casts his own poison upon those who follow him. Thus also he deceived Eve, not speaking his own things, but pretending the words of God, and falsifying their meaning. Thus also he subverted the wife of Job, persuading her to pretend devotion to her husband, but teaching her to blaspheme against God. Thus the deceitful one plays with human beings by illusions, stealing away and dragging each one into his own pit of evil. If he does not trust against his children, but against his angels he devised something crooked. Of Athanasius. But the nature of begotten and created things is changeable, since indeed it is outside the essence of God, and came into being from non-beings. Therefore every man is a liar; and, all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God. But the devil, being in the midst of the cherubim, and having become a seal-impression of likeness, fell from the heavens like lightning. And we will judge angels, namely those who did not keep their own domain. And here, if he does not trust against his children, and simply the created things have such a nature, and it changes. But only the divine nature is unchangeable. Beside papyrus, and reed, and bulrush. Perhaps through the reed and the papyrus the Scripture hints at the cheapness and the poverty of the devil. His entrails are bronze asps. Athanasius. Long ago then the enemy was great, scheming against human beings, and by his illusions he deceived many, and the detection of his deceit was difficult; so that even the Spirit says about him: Who will uncover the face of his garment? and the things following. For he was not appearing as what he was, but toward what he was scheming, toward this he also made himself appear by illusion. For this reason also many were deceived by him; but when the Savior came, then all his illusion was exposed; for the things he was doing, unknown long ago, these are known by the grace of Christ, and in the things in which he long ago deceived human beings, in these he is trampled by them. For faith is stronger than every devilish assault and madness of demons.

choices.english: the tempter was pouring forth abundantly
choices.why: ἔῤῥεεν here means abundant activity or assault, not liquid flow; 'pouring forth' captures the sense of the tempter's relentless activity.

choices.english: to pretend devotion to her husband
choices.why: φιλανδρία means wifely devotion or love of husband as a virtue; she was persuaded to feign this devotion, not to pretend love for him.
rejected: to pretend love for her husband

choices.why: ἀποσφράγισμα is the impression made by a seal, i.e., bearing God's image as stamped or sealed, not possessing a seal.
εὑρετής means inventor or deviser; 'inventor of evil' preserves the active sense of originating evil.
φαντασία is the devil's deceptive appearance; 'illusion' is the glossary term and captures the counterfeit nature.
δειγματίζω means to make a public example or expose; 'was exposed' fits the context of Christ revealing the devil's illusions.

pass_b_english: The tempter was pouring forth abundantly, and the one fighting was harsh; but the one being tempted appeared more courageous, conquering the assaults and attacks of the evil one by the greatness of his mind. The mark of courage is endurance. For by this each of the saints, bearing the painful and grievous things that happen in life, prevailed against the devil. The Spirit, wanting us to possess both, commands in the psalm: “Be strong, and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord” (Psalm 26:14 (Hebrew 27:14)). For the one who endures is courageous, and the courageous one would be enduring. Therefore blessed Job was strengthened through enduring, and through bearing his pains courageously he endured. He pushed away his wife, who had been deceived by the serpent and corrupted in her thoughts.

For since the inventor of evil is altogether a hater, and appearing only as one seeking whom he may seize and swallow, for this reason he hides and covers what he himself is. But by illusion he counterfeits the truth that all desire, and casts his own poison upon those who follow him. So he deceived Eve, not speaking his own words, but counterfeiting the words of God and corrupting their minds. So he subverted Job’s wife, persuading her to disguise herself in wifely love, but teaching her to blaspheme against God. So the deceiver plays with human beings through illusions, stealing and dragging each one into his own pit of evil.

“If he does not trust his own servants, and against his angels he has devised something crooked.” Athanasius. The nature of begotten and created things is changeable, since it is outside the being of God and came into existence from nothing. Therefore “every human being is a liar” (Psalm 116:11 (LXX 115:2)), and “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23). The devil, being in the midst of the cherubim and having become a seal of likeness, fell from heaven like lightning (Luke 10:18). And we will judge angels (1 Corinthians 6:3)—those, clearly, who did not keep their own domain (Jude 6). And here, “if he does not trust his own servants,” simply shows that created things have such a nature and are changeable. Only the divine nature is unchangeable.

“By papyrus, and reed, and bulrush.” Perhaps through the reed and the papyrus Scripture hints at the worthlessness and poverty of the devil. “His inward parts are bronze shields.” Athanasius. Long ago the enemy was great in his scheming against human beings, and by his illusions he deceived many, and the detection of his deceit was difficult—so that the Spirit says about him: “Who will uncover the face of his garment?” (Job 41:13) and so on. For he did not appear as what he was, but he produced an illusion of himself corresponding to whatever he was scheming. Therefore many were deceived by him. But when the Savior came, then all his illusion was exposed. For the things he did of old that went unrecognized are now known by the grace of Christ, and the things by which he once deceived human beings are now trampled underfoot by them. For faith is stronger than every assault of the devil and madness of demons.
notes: The source contains the lemma headings 'Ἀθανασίου' and 'Ἀθανάσιος' embedded in the text, indicating attribution to Athanasius; these are preserved in the gloss as 'Of Athanasius' and 'Athanasius'.

problems.quote: he made himself appear as whatever he was scheming toward
problems.source_quote: πρὸς ὃ ἐπανουργεύετο, πρὸς τοῦτο καὶ ἐφαντασίου ἑαυτόν
problems.why: ἐφαντασίου means 'he produced an illusion/phantasm of himself,' not 'made himself appear'; active deception, not self-appearance.
problems.fix: he produced an illusion of himself corresponding to whatever he was scheming

problems.quote: the things he was once unknown to be doing
problems.why: ἠγνοεῖτο is passive: 'the things that were unknown' (impersonal), not 'he was unknown to be doing'; subject is the things, not the devil.
problems.fix: for the things that were unknown of old that he was doing

problems.quote: the one fighting against him was harsh
problems.why: Source says the one fighting was harsh/difficult, not 'against him'; the combatant is the devil, not a neutral party.
problems.ruling: ὁ μαχόμενος is the devil, not 'one fighting against him'; context shows tempter vs. tempted.

problems.quote: and only appears seeking whom he may seize and swallow
problems.source_quote: καὶ μόνον φαινόμενος ζητῶν τίνα ἁρπάσει καὶ καταπιεῖ
problems.why: μόνον modifies φαινόμενος: 'only appearing to seek,' i.e., he merely seems to seek prey. English reads 'only appears seeking' = 'his sole activity is seeking.'
problems.fix: and appearing only to seek whom he may seize and swallow
problems.ruling: μόνον modifies φαινόμενος: 'only appearing,' not 'only appears seeking' as sole activity.

problems.why: αὐτῶν refers to Eve and Adam's understanding ('their minds'), not to the words' meaning. The devil falsified their thinking.
problems.ruling: αὐτῶν refers to Eve/Adam (τὴν Εὔαν...αὐτῶν), not 'their meaning'; devil corrupted their minds.

problems.why: The quote 'every human being is a liar' matches Psalm 116:11 (LXX 115:2) or Job, not Romans 3:4 which quotes Psalm 116.
problems.ruling: πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης is Psalm 116:11 LXX; Romans 3:4 cites it but is wrong primary reference.

fixed: Fixed 'the one fighting against him was harsh' to 'the one fighting was harsh': source has 'χαλεπὸς ἦν ὁ μαχόμενος' with no 'against him'.
Fixed 'and only appears seeking whom he may seize and swallow' to 'and appearing only to seek whom he may seize and swallow': source 'μόνον φαινόμενος ζητῶν' has μόνον modifying φαινόμενος.
Fixed 'and falsifying their meaning' to 'and corrupting their minds': source 'τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν παραποιῶν' refers to their understanding/minds, not the words' meaning.

Fixed 'he made himself appear as whatever he was scheming toward' to 'he produced an illusion of himself corresponding to whatever he was scheming': source 'ἐφαντασίου ἑαυτόν' means he produced an illusion of himself.
Fixed 'the things he was once unknown to be doing' to 'the things that were unknown of old that he was doing': source 'ἃ γὰρ ἠγνοεῖτο πάλαι ποιῶν' has passive ἠγνοεῖτο with the things as subject.
Fixed 'Romans 3:4' to 'Psalm 116:11 (LXX 115:2)': the quote 'every human being is a liar' matches Psalm 116:11 (LXX 115:2), not Romans 3:4.

problems.why: γεννητῶν here means 'created/born things' not 'begotten' in the theological sense; context contrasts all created nature with divine nature.
ἀποσφράγισμα means 'seal' or 'signet,' not 'seal-impression'; the phrase refers to being a seal of likeness, a stamped image.

edits.old: The nature of begotten and created things is changeable
edits.new: The nature of created and made things is changeable

edits.old: having become a seal-impression of likeness
edits.new: having become a seal of likeness

fixed: γεννητῶν here refers to things that have come into being, not 'begotten' in the theological sense; 'created and made things' better captures the contrast with the divine nature.
ἀποσφράγισμα means 'seal' or 'signet,' not 'seal-impression'; 'seal of likeness' is the correct rendering.

problems.why: γεννητῶν means 'begotten/offspring' not 'created'; contradicts Athanasius's argument.
ὑποκρίνεσθαι here means 'to play a part/disguise oneself as' not 'pretend devotion'; she feigned wifely love as disguise.

problems.quote: and appearing only to seek whom he may seize and swallow
problems.source_quote: καὶ μό νον φαινόμενος ζητῶν τίνα ἁρπάσει καὶ καταπιεῖ
problems.why: Source says 'appearing only to seek'; English 'and appearing only to seek' is grammatically broken—'only' modifies 'appearing', not 'seek'.
problems.fix: and appearing only as one seeking whom he may seize and swallow
problems.ruling: μόνον modifies ζητῶν, not φαινόμενος; English 'only appearing' misrepresents 'appearing only to seek'.

problems.quote: the things that were unknown of old that he was doing
problems.why: Source means 'the things that were unknown when he was doing them of old'; English is ungrammatical and unclear.
problems.fix: for the things he did of old that went unrecognized
problems.ruling: ἃ γὰρ ἠγνοεῖτο πάλαι ποιῶν: 'the things he did of old that were unknown'; English word order obscures temporal sense.

problems.why: LXX Psalm numbering is 30:25, but Hebrew is 31:24; LXX should be primary citation per brief.
problems.ruling: Source says ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ with no number; adding both Psalm 31:24 and LXX 30:25 is a translator's reference, not a source error.

fixed: γεννητῶν means 'begotten/offspring', not 'created'; 'begotten and created things' is correct.
ὑποκρίνεσθαι φιλανδρίαν means to disguise oneself in wifely love, not merely pretend devotion.

Source: 'ἃ γὰρ ἠγνοεῖτο πάλαι ποιῶν' — 'the things he did of old that went unrecognized' is accurate.

fixed.note: The singular 'ἀνδρίζου … καὶ ὑπόμεινον τὸν Κύριον' is Psalm 26:14 LXX; Psalm 30:25 is plural and lacks 'wait for the Lord', and the site uses LXX-first format.

dismissed.why: ὑποκρίνεσθαι means 'to play a role, feign, counterfeit,' not 'disguise herself.' The devil made her feign wifely love to deceive Job.
dismissed.note: 'Disguise herself in wifely love' already conveys pretense, so the change to 'feign' is a matter of style.
